content:
Apple is about to launch its flagship new iPhones: the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone Ultra. The price will be a clear advantage for the Pro series, but the iPhone 18 Pro also outshines the more expensive Ultra model in several other areas.

#1: Main camera with variable aperture

The iPhone 18 Pro's main camera is rumoured to undergo major changes, including an upgrade to a variable aperture. The iPhone Ultra, however, is not expected to get this feature.

Rumours about a variable aperture have been circulating for a long time, but we still don't know exactly how Apple plans to implement it. It could bring significant improvements to Portrait mode and offer deeper depth-of-field control. Night-time photography performance could also see a major boost.

The components required for a variable aperture are expected to be larger than the current main camera. Therefore, the ultra-thin iPhone Ultra is believed to miss out on this feature.

#2: Even longer battery life on Pro Max

Based on regulatory filings, the iPhone Ultra should offer decent battery life. But the Pro series — that is, the iPhone 18 Pro Max — will still deliver the longest battery life of any iPhone yet.

The iPhone 18 Pro Max is reported to feature a physical battery that is 10% larger than that of the iPhone 17 Pro Max. It will also benefit from efficiency gains brought by the A20 Pro and C2 chips. As a result, battery life should easily be the best ever on an iPhone.

Due to its unique foldable design, it's hard to judge the iPhone Ultra's battery life from specs alone. But the ultra-thin design and smaller physical battery will no doubt prevent it from catching up with the iPhone 18 Pro Max.

#3: Face ID

For the first time in many years, a flagship new iPhone model will not feature Face ID. Instead, the iPhone Ultra will only support Touch ID.

Meanwhile, the iPhone 18 Pro will continue to use the Face ID system that has been around for nearly a decade.

Apple is reportedly unable to make room for the Face ID components in the ultra-thin iPhone Ultra design. Proper support would require two sets of components — one for the outer display and another for the inner display. So when it comes to authentication, the iPhone 18 Pro will have a clear edge.

#4: Telephoto camera

The iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max will continue to be the only models equipped with a telephoto camera. The iPhone Ultra will have a main camera and an ultra-wide camera, but no telephoto camera for optical zoom.

For many users who rely on telephoto capabilities, this could be a major difference. Especially since Apple is rumoured to be further enhancing the telephoto camera this year with a larger aperture.

If you're after the most advanced camera system, the iPhone 18 Pro is the obvious choice.

Bonus: The traditional iPhone experience

This isn't a technical feature, but it's worth mentioning. For many users, the iPhone 18 Pro offering a "traditional" iPhone experience will be an advantage.

The iPhone Ultra will be unlike any model that has come before it. The size and shape of both the inner and outer displays will feel unfamiliar for an iPhone. Instead of simply using one screen, you'll need to fold and unfold it, which may take some getting used to.

The current iPhone form factor is a product that users love. While foldables do have plenty of fans, I'd wager that for the average consumer (who may have never even heard of 9to5Mac), the iPhone 18 Pro's traditional iPhone design is what will appeal to many.

Which new iPhone model are you planning to buy this autumn? Let us know in the comments.
